big_idea: We check our model against reality. If it is off, we REFINE it — predictions improve with practice.
learning_intention: We are learning to check our prediction against what really happens and adjust the model.
student_learning_goal: I can check my prediction against what really happens and adjust the model.
success_criteria: I can compare a prediction to actual data.
I can describe whether my model needs to be refined.
I can suggest how to refine the model.
lesson_specific_materials: Per-pair prediction chart with PREDICT and ACTUAL columns
Lesson 4 reflection tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Sap Sam predicted 5 buckets but only got 4. What does that mean?
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Maple + Sap Sam puppets. 'Friends — yesterday Sap Sam PREDICTED. Today we CHECK whether his predictions matched reality.'

'Sap Sam predicted 5 buckets for 5 trees. He went to the bush. He got... 4 buckets. One tree was DRY.'

Write on the chart:
Predict: 5
Actual: 4
Difference: 1 less

'What does this mean? Was Sap Sam wrong?'

Lead the discussion: 'Predictions are GUESSES based on rules. Sometimes reality is different. We REFINE — improve — our model with new data.'

Write REFINE on the chart. 'Sap Sam refines his rule: maybe ONE in every five trees is dry. So for 10 trees, predict 8 (not 10).'

Now another. 'Sap Sam predicts 8 buckets. Goes to bush. Gets 9. ONE EXTRA bucket — the rain made an extra-flowing tree.' Refine: 'Sometimes more, sometimes less. Use a RANGE.'

'Today we'll predict, check, and refine. Not just one prediction — many.'
student_actions: Suggest how to refine the rule.

steps.instruction: Whole group: predict-and-check 4 more scenarios. (a) 6 trees → predict 6, actual 5. (b) 8 trees → predict 8, actual 8. (c) 10 trees → predict 10, actual 11. (d) 4 trees → predict 4, actual 3.

Send pairs to three stations (~7 min each). Station A: Predict-and-Check — pair predicts 3 sap-bucket scenarios with given data; teacher reveals actual; pair refines. Station B: Refine the Rule — pair gets a rule that's a bit off ('1 tree = 1 bucket'); refine to '4 of 5 trees = 1 bucket each'. Station C: Real-Life Refinement — pair refines a real-life prediction (e.g., 'My class always has 24 — but Wednesday someone is sick — refine to 23').
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Three stations, 7 minutes each.'

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge at Station C: invent a rule that always works. Discuss whether perfect rules exist. Most rules need refinement.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to pairs: 'Most rules need refinement. Few rules are perfect.'

steps.instruction: Discuss the cycle. 'Modelling is a CYCLE. We predict, check, refine, predict again. Each round we improve.'
steps.teacher_prompt: Show the modelling cycle chart with arrows pointing back to PREDICT.

steps.instruction: Circulate to record formative evidence on the reflection tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'What's your refinement?' Mark the tracker.

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Use only simple predict-vs-actual scenarios.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch at Station C: refine a complex multi-rule model.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide structured frame: 'I predicted ___. Actual was ___. I refine to ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk through a physical predict-act-check loop.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: compares prediction to actual; describes the gap; suggests a refinement.
formative_check.how_to_record: Tick the reflection tracker per child.

discussion_prompts: Why don't predictions always match reality?
How does refining make our model better?
What's a real-life rule you'd refine?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child writes ONE refinement on a sticky note: 'I'd refine my rule to ___.' Notes go on the chart.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 4 captures the REFLECT step of the modelling cycle.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says 'My prediction was WRONG' instead of 'I need to refine my model' — repairing the wrong-vs-imperfect framing
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on REFLECT is the wrong-vs-refine framing: the child treats a missed prediction as a personal failure ('I was wrong') rather than as a data point that improves the model ('I need to refine my rule').

The walkthrough covers the precise moment when a child feels bad about a missed prediction.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. The child predicted 5 buckets, actual was 4. The child says 'I was wrong.'
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch beside the child. 'You weren't WRONG — your model was IMPERFECT. That's totally normal. Maple says — every prediction teaches us. We REFINE.'

'Refining is GROWING — your model gets better with each round. The first prediction is a guess; later ones are smarter.'

Long-term recovery: normalize imperfect predictions. Praise the refinement.
expected_student_responses: (Confused) Treats missed prediction as personal failure.
(Mid) Acknowledges with prompts; doesn't yet auto-frame as refinement.
(Strong) Says 'I'll refine my model' or 'next time I'll predict ___'.
(Stretched) Volunteers multiple refinements based on trends.
common_misconceptions: Wrong predictions = wrong me. (Repair: imperfect models are expected.)
Refinement is failure. (Repair: refinement is growth.)
Models should be perfect from the start. (Repair: iterative improvement is the goal.)
recovery_moves: Celebrate the iteration. 'Round 2 prediction is smarter.'
Show the cycle's looping arrows. Continual improvement.

parts_outline.task: Reflect on a real-life prediction you made. Did it match? How would you refine?
